subject: Onboarding benchmark: acceptance criteria and run cadence
messages:
From: Matt Johnson <matt.johnson@fastgro.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Onboarding benchmark: acceptance criteria and next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We want to get a formal acceptance run scheduled so engineering can validate costs and SLA fit before we flip traffic. A few quick items from our side:

- Target throughput: ~500 requests/sec sustained (we can ramp).
- Latency target: p95 < 200ms for the typical 256-token prompt mix.
- Tail: we care about p99 under load (please surface tail latency).
- Test window: prefer a daytime run on Tue/Wed next week (PST).

Can you share your proposed load test script, a short runbook (what you need from our side), and how you’ll share results? Also: do you need production-like payloads or is synthetic sufficient for first pass?

Opening the calendar: ops@fastgro.com and I are on this thread.

Thanks,
Matt
Matt Johnson | Head of Platform Engineering
FastGro Inc.
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Matt Johnson <matt.johnson@fastgro.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: acceptance criteria and run cadence

Thanks Matt — great to see alignment on targets. Quick reply with a proposed stitch plan and attached artifacts.

High-level acceptance criteria (proposed)
- Throughput: sustained 500 req/s for 30m steady state with <5% error rate.
- Latency: p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms across the 256-token payload mix.
- Stability: no memory/gpu OOMs, <1% transient 5xx errors, and KV cache hit rates documented.

Planned test cadence (proposal)
1) Dry run (synthetic): Thu 2025-03-24 09:00 PST — smoke + ramp to 250 req/s to validate scripts and endpoints.
2) Full day acceptance run: Tue 2025-03-25 09:00 PST — ramp to 500 req/s, two 30m steady windows separated by a warmup.
3) Post-run analysis: we’ll share raw telemetry and a CSV summary within 24 hours; then we sync for signoff.

What we need from FastGro
- Production-like payloads (sample JSON with 1–3 prompt variants) OR confirmation we can use the attached synthetic mix.
- Whitelisted IPs (we’ll provide a short list) or temporary bearer token for the test.
- Point of contact for network/infra on the day of the run (ops@fastgro.com is fine).

Attachments included in this message: redwood-onboard-runbook-v1.pdf (runbook + roles), load-script-fastgro-20250324.yml (k6/JMeter style), latency-results-template.csv (summary template).

Ben/Monica — I’m looping you in for telemetry and post-run artifact ownership. Ben, can you confirm the data we’ll collect (token-level timing, gpu utilization, error traces) and whether we want extra traces at p99+?

Matt — if the cadence above looks OK I’ll lock the slots and share a Drive folder + a Doc with expected payloads.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Matt Johnson <matt.johnson@fastgro.com>
Date: 2025-03-23T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: acceptance criteria and run cadence

Echoing Marissa — a few telemetry notes from infra side:

Telemetry we will collect (minimum)
- Token-level timing (request start, first-byte, last-byte).
- Per-request GPU utilization and memory snapshots (sampled every 30s).
- Error classification (4xx/5xx with stack traces where available).
- KV cache hit/miss rates and prefix cache effectiveness.

Extra asks for FastGro
- If you can provide 500–1,000 sample production-like requests (anonymized), that will make p99 a lot more indicative.
- If any requests involve long-context (>1024 tokens) call that out — we’ll run a smaller set to validate stateful/kv behaviour.

Data retention & sharing
- We’ll upload raw traces to the shared Drive folder and provide a CSV summary (latency buckets, error rates, throughput timeline).
- If you prefer an S3 transfer instead, provide a presigned path and we’ll push artifacts there.

I’ll also add a short postmortem template to the Drive so we can capture any anomalies during the run (time, symptom, mitigation).

—Ben
Ben Carter | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Matt Johnson <matt.johnson@fastgro.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, ops@fastgro.com
Date: 2025-03-25T15:54:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Onboarding benchmark: acceptance criteria and run cadence — confirmed

Matt / team — schedule confirmed. Quick summary and next steps:

- Dry run: 2025-03-24 09:00 PST (synthetic) — completed successfully (scripts validated).
- Acceptance run: 2025-03-25 09:00 PST — ran two 30m steady windows, peak sustained 520 req/s, p95 measured 185ms, p99 380ms.
- Attachments uploaded to Drive: latency-results-template.csv (populated), full-telemetry.tar.gz (raw traces), redwood-onboard-runbook-v1.pdf.

Initial readout: both steady windows met the proposed acceptance thresholds (throughput and p95). We saw three short-lived 5xx spikes during the second ramp — Ben captured traces and we’ve filed a follow-up ticket (INF-7321) which is linked in the Drive.

Next steps
- Ben to share the short postmortem and the raw p99 trace snippets (ETA: 24 hours).
- If FastGro signs off on these runs, we’ll schedule a final configuration handoff and recommend a quantization profile for cost savings.
- Marissa to open the SOW amendment for production cutover once signoff received.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cFastGroBenchmark (artifacts), https://app.redwood.com/s/DEAL-2025-0457 (deal record).

Thanks everyone — great collaboration.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
